bioAdditions:
The printed Brookhaven town records add detail to James's Long Island years. On 1 May 1721 land was laid out to him on the other half of Dayton's Right, next to his Chestnut Pound land and his 'former 50 lot'. This is the Dayton's Right land his brother John (d. 1743) also referred to (S1, S2). In June 1737 he owned the westernmost 15-acre lot in Fireplace Neck 'at South', and a new highway was laid along the north ends of those lots at his request and his neighbours' (S1). A 'James Tuttle, junr.' signs a town paper c.1738/9. On Alva Tuttle's list he is the son James b. 1717, later of New Windsor (d. 1756) (S1, S4). In October 1741 James sat as one of four arbitrators in a town dispute (S1). Fireplace Neck lies a few miles west of Moriches, the home of James Smith and Jerusha Topping, whose daughter Temperance married James's son John in 1752.

The tree gives James's wife as 'Hannah S. Reeve (1699-1764)'. Akerly (1898) shows that Hannah, daughter of Maj. James Reeve of Mattituck (d. 8 Mar 1764, aged 64), was the wife of James's brother **Joshua** Tuthill of Cutchogue (S2). The tree has transferred Joshua's wife and her gravestone to James. James's wife was Rachel Browne (Alva Tuttle p. 279, via S4).

conflicts.foundValue: Akerly 1898: Hannah, dau. of Maj. James Reeve, d. 8 Mar 1764 ae. 64, was wife of Joshua Tuthill (b. 1690) of Cutchogue
conflicts.assessment: Tree error: Joshua's wife was attached to James. Keep Rachel Browne as James's wife.
